body.statement: Using \(\mathsf{Refine}\), can one construct a concrete serialized parser, generator, and executable exact-rational checker that refines \(\operatorname{Gen}\) and \(\operatorname{Verify}\) and prove, for every well-formed \(I\in\mathfrak I_{q,k}^{\ge3}\), the soundness, generator completeness, rational endpoint realization, and \(2^{O(q^2(k+1)^2)}\operatorname{poly}(B)\) bit bound asserted in \(\text{thm:verifier-refinement}\), while replaying \(\mathsf F_\star\) and rejecting a deleted necessary vertex, a corrupted separator entry, a singular-support misclassification, and a source-kernel mismatch?
body.justification: This is the load-bearing open content: the abstract finite algorithm must survive serialization, parser, arithmetic, and decoder refinement without weakening the causal guarantee.
body.gap: Li, Passmore, and Paulson establish the producer--checker architecture for univariate algebra, while causaloptim-lean covers linear causal certificates; neither supplies this multiblock support-and-separator refinement.
body.consumer: A portable certificate artifact can be independently replayed by causal-bound software and by a later proof-assistant implementation.

obligation.what_is_open: A concrete byte-level parser, normalized-rational implementation, certificate generator, and executable checker refining \(\mathsf{Refine}\), together with adversarial rejection tests for a deleted vertex, corrupted separator row, singular-support misclassification, and source-kernel mismatch.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen core defines total mathematical functions \(\operatorname{Gen}\) and \(\operatorname{Verify}\), but supplies no concrete program or refinement relation.  The available exact checker audits the cubic support domains, endpoint models, and interleaved kernel only; it has no separator-certificate parser or corruption-test path.  Therefore abstract soundness cannot establish correctness of a nonexistent executable serialization layer.
obligation.attempted: Ran the supplied independent exact checker on the cubic and interleaved-parent computations and inspected its verification scope.  It reproduced all reported counts and fractions, but contains no serialized verifier, separator replay, deletion mutation, corruption mutation, or singular-support acceptance interface.
obligation.partial_result:
The abstract finite algorithms already satisfy the mathematical implication
\[
\operatorname{Verify}(I,\operatorname{Gen}(I))=1,
\qquad
\operatorname{Verify}(I,\Gamma)=1
\Longrightarrow
\bigl\{Q(M_0):M_0\in\mathcal M(G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\bigr\}
\subseteq[\underline\theta,\overline\theta],
\]
with rational finite SCMs attaining both endpoints and with \(2^{O(q^2(k+1)^2)}\operatorname{poly}(B)\) mathematical generation and replay cost.  Exact independent fixture computation confirms \(8192\) canonical tuples, \(4096\) cubic monomials, \(64\) positive cells, factor-vertex counts \(80\) and \(32\), \(243\) projected tuples, endpoints \(11/64\) and \(53/64\), and the interleaved-parent kernel \(1/4\) versus ordinary conditional \(3/8\).  What remains is refinement of a particular byte-level parser, rational-arithmetic implementation, generator, and adversarial certificate test suite to these abstract algorithms.
